problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${A}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $C$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${C}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[C\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 15 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We write down $C$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $C$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[C\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 15 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-7){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 15 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${C}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{C}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}15 & -7 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
